system.summary: Łaski's graphic cipher (System B of the volume): one sign per letter (21 letter signs, W serving c and t), a few word signs (DAG = King John, BIGX = Ferdinand, FLW probably King John's title), no word division marks beyond spaces. In R9403 (1531) the signs for e and r are the other way round and some shapes differ; on R9417 p.1 the raw decode shows the same e/r exchange.
system.sibling_key: none: the key was rebuilt from the glosses on R9322 and R9417 (sysB/key_from_glosses.tsv) and applied to R9323 and R9403
system.notes: Measured distinct signs: R9322 33, R9417 23, R9323 25, R9403 22 (reconstructed from its reading). Split on 15 Oct 2026 from kaa4591 (R9322, R9323, R9417) and kaa4591b (R9403) under the one-key rule.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the four letters in Łaski's System B (R9322, R9323, R9417 from kaa4591; R9403 from kaa4591b) gathered into this entry; R9414 (system G) moved to wardein1537 and R9415 (system L) to sperantio1534, whose key it shares. Words re-counted per letter (measure_sysb.py; R9403 r9403/decoded.txt).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 862 tokens, 21 types, la order 4: reading -2.091 per letter; random keys -6.002 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.682 (mean -3.757, z 37.1); annealer on the real text -2.091. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): sign files and page tsv per letter, sysB/decoded.txt, sysB/R9323_decoded.txt, r9403/decoded.txt; key sysB/key_from_glosses.tsv.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the four decodes read through. R9322 and R9403 build Latin sentences (kept read, reviewed B); R9417 has systematic letter slips in most words of half the letter and R9323 a doubtful sign in nearly every line, both relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.953 -> 0.693.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b20): every file on DECODE R9417 (2 images) and R9323 (1 image) fetched with the shared cookie (b20_fetch.py; scratchpad only). No attachments or DOC_* texts; the only contemporary text is the faint interlinear gloss (R9417 P2 ll. 1-14 and P1 ll. 5-7, R9323 ll. 1-3 and 11).

R9417 P2 image has 29 cipher lines; the transcription held 21. Lines 15-29 and P1 read sign by sign on native crops (sysB/R9417_signs_b20.tsv). The decode's 'm for a, e for r' slips were coding slips: on ll. 15-21 the dotted/plain circles and plain/starred crosses had been coded the other way round from the glossed lines 12-14, where the gloss fixes dotted circle a, plain circle m, plain x r, starred x e (the R9403 exchange). R9323 re-read word by word (11 corrections, sysB/R9323_corrections.tsv): l. 3 begins with the Ferdinand word sign; Ƶ = q, I-sign = b, dagger = n.

Readings and translations written (sysB/R9417_reading.md, R9323_reading.md, _en.md; log sysB/R9417-R9323_reread_log.md); every word carried by its signs or the gloss, doubtful words [?]. b17_score.py la: R9417 0.250 full list / 0.893 explicit holes, R9323 0.111 / 0.889 (the checker's Latin list lacks common words, -cia spellings and names). Both set read, grade B. New content: Minkuics to meet the dukes' envoys at Coburg on 4 July; the Polish king's daughter sought through Sigismund Herberstein for Frederick the Count Palatine; the dukes to ask Charles V to hold back Ferdinand.

texts.label: R9322, ff. 121-122, Buda 24 Nov 1529

reading_review.note: sysB/decoded.txt R9322 p1-p2 read through: continuous Latin sentences (the King thanks the duke for his counsel; the Sultan withdrew for the plague and left the kingdom of Hungary to King John; King John's letter for the Jew Lazarus) with single-letter slips and a few [D]/[X] name signs; only the last lines of p2 (address, scipsit) are garbled.

texts.summary: f. 121: Hieronymus Łaski to a Bavarian duke, Buda 24 Nov 1529: the Sultan, forced home by plague in his army, left King John the kingdom of Hungary without tribute, with fifty guns and powder, and will return next summer against Ferdinand's lands unless there is a concord. f. 122: King John of Hungary to Duke Ludwig of Bavaria, sending Lazarus the Jew as envoy.

texts.label: R9417, f. 264, Kraków 16 June [1530]
texts.summary: Łaski to the dukes' secretary Waisenfelder, Kraków 16 June [1530]: concord best made through the imperial princes; Nicolaus Minkuics sent to the King of France and to meet the dukes' envoys at Coburg on 4 July (the roads were beset); the Sultan, persuaded to a year's truce, will receive whom King John names and will come next summer by land and sea unless there is concord; the King of Poland's daughter: the match starts coldly while someone presses through Sigismund Herberstein for Frederick the Count Palatine; the dukes should send to Charles V to hold back his brother from attacking King John. Signed 'Lask', in his own hand.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b20): P2 ll. 15-29 and P1 read sign by sign at the image; the transcription had stopped at l. 21 and coded the two circle and two cross shapes the other way round from the glossed lines (gloss: dotted circle a, plain circle m, plain x r, starred x e, the R9403 exchange); ll. 1-14 follow the decode and the gloss. Every word carried by its signs or the gloss; 16 doubtful words [?], one owl word sign and one word unread. b17_score.py la: 0.250 (7/28) on the full list (it lacks carissime, arripere, nominabit, -cia spellings, names), explicit holes 0.893 (25/28).

texts.label: R9323, f. 123, [1529-30]
texts.summary: Latin note from Łaski's circle to the Bavarian secretary: [FLW] loves the Duke of Bavaria; Łaski wants concord between King John and Ferdinand, for without it Bohemia will perish and the Turks will consume it and Austria; the other princes' lands have nothing to fear by his pact with the Turk unless the Imperial estates aid Ferdinand against [FLW]; the Turks are not to be despised; he would have sent horses to the Sultan; commends himself to the dukes.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b20): re-read word by word at the image; l. 3 begins with the Ferdinand word sign (not an unknown XC), Ƶ = q, the I-sign = b, the dagger = n; 11 transcription corrections (R9323_corrections.tsv). Two faint words of l. 10 unread; three doubtful. b17_score.py la: 0.111 (1/9) on the full list, explicit holes 0.889 (8/9).

texts.label: R9403, ff. 226-228, Łask 17 Sept 1531

reading_review.note: r9403/decoded.txt read through: continuous Latin (Łaski thanks for the letters brought by Ruffus; the Turk's answer to King Ferdinand's envoys: no peace unless he cedes Hungary to King John) with rare slips; the audit row did not read this letter.

texts.summary: Łaski to a councillor of the Bavarian dukes, 17 Sept 1531: the Sultan told Ferdinand's envoys there would be no peace or truce unless Hungary is given up to King John, and is preparing ships, guns and grain on the Danube; Łaski will ride to the Speyer diet and asks the dukes to stop any decision against the king; the royal marriage will be settled with the King of Poland.
